title: Flat finitely presented field cover of a singleton stack
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\mathcal Z$ an algebraic stack over $S$. Assume $\mathcal Z$ admits a smooth surjective scheme atlas that is reduced and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], where reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents. Assume $|\mathcal Z|$ has exactly one point, with field-valued objects identified when they become isomorphic over a common field extension. There exist a field $K$ [def-weil-field] and a representable-by-algebraic-spaces surjective flat locally finitely presented morphism $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal Z$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No condition on the diagonal beyond representability, and no Noetherian condition on $S$, is assumed. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre products and representability use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable maps are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts after a field extension.

proof.text: Choose a nonempty affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ in the given atlas, small enough that $R$ is Noetherian. This is possible by the locally Noetherian hypothesis; $W\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth by source locality. The ring $R$ is nonzero and reduced, since the atlas is nonempty and reduced and sections of a reduced scheme are reduced. Choose a prime $\mathfrak p$ minimal over the proper ideal $0$. The minimal-prime localization lemma makes $E=R_{\mathfrak p}$ a field. For the point $\eta\in W$ corresponding to $\mathfrak p$, the affine stalk identification gives $\mathcal O_{W,\eta}=E$.

source.place: Tags 06MN (lemma-unique-point), (1) implies (2), and 06MP (lemma-unique-point-better), (1) implies (2); algebra.tex Tags 00E0(3) and 00EU; schemes.tex Tags 01J1 and 01HV(6).

proof.text: The canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}E=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,\eta}\to W$ is flat by the spectrum-of-stalk lemma. Smoothness makes $W\to\mathcal Z$ flat, so their composite $b:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\mathcal Z$ is flat. It is representable by algebraic spaces because its source is a scheme and the diagonal of $\mathcal Z$ is representable. It is surjective in the required sense: any field-valued object of $\mathcal Z$ and $b$ represent its unique point, so over a common field extension they become isomorphic; the extension of $b$ is the required lift.

source.place: Tag 06MN (lemma-unique-point), (1) implies (2); representability is algebraic.tex Tag 045G.

proof.text: Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of the nonzero ring $R$ and put $K=R/\mathfrak m$, a field by the quotient-field lemma. Since $R$ is Noetherian, write $\mathfrak m=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$. The map $R\to K=R/(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ is finitely presented by the defining presentation with zero polynomial generators. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}K\to W$ is locally of finite presentation by the affine definition. Smoothness of $W\to\mathcal Z$ and composition give a locally finitely presented map $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\mathcal Z$. Its scheme source makes it representable by algebraic spaces. The same common-field-extension argument as in step 2 makes $a$ surjective. We still have to prove its flatness; the closed point map to $W$ need not be flat.

source.place: Tag 06MP (lemma-unique-point-better), (1) implies (2), closed-point construction; morphisms.tex Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation), applied directly to the finitely generated maximal ideal (the argument behind Tag 01TV).

proof.text: Form the algebraic space $T=\operatorname{Spec}E\times_{\mathcal Z}\operatorname{Spec}K$, with projections $p:T\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and $q:T\to\operatorname{Spec}E$. The map $p$ is flat and surjective by base change of $b$. The map $q$ is flat: on an etale surjective scheme chart $U\to T$, the scheme morphism $U\to\operatorname{Spec}E$ is flat by the cited field-base flatness lemma. The algebraic-space chart criterion therefore applies to $q$. Consequently $c=bq:T\to\mathcal Z$, which is 2-isomorphic to $ap$, is flat by composition.

source.place: Tag 06MM (lemma-flat-cover-by-field), fibre square and flatness over the field; flatness is tested on etale scheme charts (spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03MJ and 03MM).

proof.text: We descend this flatness using schemes, without any quasi-compactness assertion about $p$. Fix any scheme $V\to\mathcal Z$ and an etale surjective scheme chart $Q\to A_V=\operatorname{Spec}K\times_{\mathcal Z}V$. Put $T_V=T\times_{\mathcal Z}V$ and $D=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}Q$. The identity $D\simeq T_V\times_{A_V}Q$ makes $D\to T_V$ etale. Choose an etale surjective scheme chart $P\to D$. The scheme map $P\to Q$ is flat and surjective: $D\to Q$ is a base change of $p$, followed by the etale cover $P\to D$. Also $P\to V$ is flat: it factors through the etale maps $P\to D\to T_V$ and the flat base change $T_V\to V$ of $c$. Apply scheme flat source descent to $P\to Q\to V$ to get $Q\to V$ flat. The algebraic-space chart test gives $A_V\to V$ flat. Since $V\to\mathcal Z$ was arbitrary, $a$ is flat by the stated convention for representable morphisms. Together with step 3 this proves every requested property.
